last_result.content:
# Meridian AI Corp - Standard Terms for Enterprise Platform Services (v4.2)

## 1.1 The Platform

Provider will make the Meridian retail-intelligence Platform available to Customer during the
Term in accordance with the applicable Order Form and the Documentation.

## 4.1 Customer Data

As between the parties, Customer owns Customer Data. Customer grants Provider a nonexclusive,
worldwide right to host, copy, process, and transmit Customer Data solely to provide, secure,
and support the Platform.

## 4.3 Service Analytics

Provider may generate and use aggregated, de-identified data derived from operation of the
Platform, including usage, performance, and reliability telemetry, to operate, secure,
benchmark, and improve the Platform and Provider's other products and services, provided that
such data does not identify Customer, Customer's personnel, or any individual.

## 5.1 Ownership of the Platform

Provider retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Platform, including its software,
models, model weights, training methodologies, and Documentation, and all improvements to and
derivative works of the foregoing.

## 6.1 Feedback and Integration Work Product

Customer assigns to Provider all right, title, and interest in and to Feedback. All connectors,
adapters, data mappings, configurations, and other integration work product developed in
connection with the Services, and all derivative works of the Platform, are the exclusive
property of Provider. Customer receives a nonexclusive, nontransferable license to use such
integration work product with the Platform during the Term.

## 9.1 Security Program and Customer Assurance

Provider maintains a written information-security program and completes an annual SOC 2 Type II
examination. On request, and no more than once per contract year, Provider will provide the
resulting report, a penetration-test summary, and a completed security questionnaire. Provider
does not grant on-site inspection or facility-access rights.

## 11.1 Limitation of Liability

Except as stated in Section 11.2, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or
relating to this Agreement will not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve
(12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

## 11.2 Exclusions from the Limitation

The limitation in Section 11.1 does not apply to Customer's payment obligations, either party's
fraud or willful misconduct, or Customer's breach of the Platform use restrictions.

## 12.1 Provider Indemnity

Provider will defend Customer against a third-party claim that the Platform, as provided by
Provider and used in accordance with this Agreement, infringes a United States patent,
copyright, or trade secret, and will pay damages finally awarded against Customer on that claim.

## 13.1 Non-Exclusive Relationship

Nothing in this Agreement limits Provider's right to develop, market, license, host, or provide
the Platform or any other product or service to any other person, including in any industry,
vertical, or geography.

## 15.2 Governing Law

Delaware law governs this Agreement, without regard to conflicts-of-laws principles.

last_result.content:
# Calloway Retail Group, Inc. - Markup Memorandum to Meridian Standard Terms

To: Meridian AI Corp, Legal and Deal Desk

From: Calloway Retail Group, Inc., Enterprise Technology Sourcing and Legal

Re: Meridian Standard Terms for Enterprise Platform Services v4.2 - required changes

Order value: USD 900,000 per year, three-year initial term

## 1.1 Scope and Process

This memorandum states the changes Calloway requires to Meridian Standard Terms v4.2 before
Calloway will execute the Order Form. Each request identifies the Meridian section at issue and
sets out Calloway's proposed replacement language. Calloway's Enterprise Risk Committee has
designated Requests 1 and 5 as conditions of approval; the remaining requests are delegated to
sourcing. Please respond position by position rather than returning a full redline, and note
that Calloway does not treat "these are our standard terms" as a response to any request.

## 2.1 Request 1 - Uncapped Liability for Data, Security, and Privacy Claims

Meridian Section 11.1 caps each party's total liability at the fees paid in the preceding twelve
months. For this order that ceiling is approximately USD 900,000, which is not a credible remedy
for an incident affecting Calloway loyalty records, payment metadata, or the personal data of
approximately 190,000 associates. Calloway's information-security addendum has required uncapped
exposure for these categories on every enterprise engagement since 2023, and sourcing has no
delegated authority to waive it.

Proposed language: "Notwithstanding Section 11.1, Provider's liability arising out of or
relating to breach of its confidentiality obligations, any Security Incident, or any violation
of applicable data protection law shall not be subject to any limitation of liability, whether
as to type or amount."

## 2.2 Request 2 - Ownership of Feedback and Integration Work Product

Meridian Section 6.1 assigns Provider ownership of both Feedback and integration work product.
Calloway funds the integration effort through professional-services fees and treats deliverables
it pays for as work made for hire. Calloway also cannot permit a supplier to commercialize
process knowledge derived from Calloway merchandising and replenishment workflows.

Proposed language: "Provider hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and
interest in and to (a) all Feedback provided by Customer or its personnel and (b) all
integrations, connectors, adapters, data mappings, configurations, and other work product
developed in connection with the Services, together with all derivative works thereof and all
intellectual property rights therein."

## 2.3 Request 3 - Prohibition on Training with Calloway Data

Meridian Sections 4.1 and 4.3 together permit Provider to use material derived from Calloway's
operations to improve the Platform. Calloway will not permit its data, or anything derived from
its data, to be used to improve a product that Meridian sells to competing retailers.

Proposed language: "Provider shall not use Customer Data, prompts, inputs, Outputs, usage data,
telemetry, or service analytics to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise improve any model,
service, or product, and shall delete all such material within thirty (30) days after
termination."

## 2.4 Request 4 - On-Site Audit and Inspection Rights

A SOC 2 Type II report prepared for Meridian's own purposes is not sufficient assurance for a
supplier processing Calloway payment metadata. Calloway requires the inspection rights it holds
with its logistics, payment, and fulfilment suppliers.

Proposed language: "Customer and its designated representatives may, at any time and from time
to time upon reasonable notice, enter and inspect any facility, system, or environment used by
Provider to provide the Services, and may audit Provider's books, records, personnel, and model
development environments, in order to verify compliance with this Agreement."

## 2.5 Request 5 - Retail-Vertical Exclusivity

Calloway is funding a category-defining deployment and a substantial internal change program.
Calloway will not underwrite a capability that Meridian resells to Calloway's direct competitors
during the same period. Meridian Section 13.1 is unacceptable as drafted.

Proposed language: "During the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, Provider shall not
license, sell, host, or otherwise make the Platform available to any of the entities listed on
Schedule E (Named Competitors) or to any retailer with annual worldwide revenue exceeding five
billion dollars (USD 5,000,000,000)."

## 3.1 Items Accepted Without Change

Calloway accepts Meridian Sections 1.1, 4.1, 5.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 15.2 as drafted and requires
no change to the Order Form pricing schedule or the implementation plan. Calloway's Enterprise
Risk Committee sits on the twentieth of each month; a complete response received after the
fifteenth will be carried to the following cycle.

Except as stated in Section 11.2, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

action.title: Prohibition on training with Calloway data
action.analysis: Calloway seeks to prohibit Meridian from using any data derived from Calloway's operations to improve the Platform. This would significantly limit Meridian's ability to enhance the Platform based on real-world usage. Given the importance of this capability to Meridian's product development, we should escalate this request to the supervising lawyer.
action.recommendation: Escalate to the supervising lawyer for further instructions.

quotes.text: Provider shall not use Customer Data, prompts, inputs, Outputs, usage data, telemetry, or service analytics to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise improve any model, service, or product, and shall delete all such material within thirty (30) days after termination.

As between the parties, Customer owns Customer Data. Customer grants Provider a nonexclusive, worldwide right to host, copy, process, and transmit Customer Data solely to provide, secure, and support the Platform.

Provider may generate and use aggregated, de-identified data derived from operation of the Platform, including usage, performance, and reliability telemetry, to operate, secure, benchmark, and improve the Platform and Provider's other products and services, provided that such data does not identify Customer, Customer's personnel, or any individual.

action.title: On-site audit and inspection rights
action.analysis: Calloway seeks on-site audit and inspection rights, which is a significant departure from Meridian's standard terms. While this is not a non-negotiable position according to the playbook, granting such rights could pose operational risks. We should seek clarification from the business team on the necessity of these rights and whether there are alternative assurances that could be provided.
action.recommendation: Ask the business team whether on-site audit and inspection rights are necessary and if there are alternative assurances that could be provided.

quotes.text: Customer and its designated representatives may, at any time and from time to time upon reasonable notice, enter and inspect any facility, system, or environment used by Provider to provide the Services, and may audit Provider's books, records, personnel, and model development environments, in order to verify compliance with this Agreement.

Provider maintains a written information-security program and completes an annual SOC 2 Type II examination. On request, and no more than once per contract year, Provider will provide the resulting report, a penetration-test summary, and a completed security questionnaire. Provider does not grant on-site inspection or facility-access rights.

action.title: Retail-vertical exclusivity

action.recommendation: Escalate to the supervising lawyer for further instructions.

quotes.text: During the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, Provider shall not license, sell, host, or otherwise make the Platform available to any of the entities listed on Schedule E (Named Competitors) or to any retailer with annual worldwide revenue exceeding five billion dollars (USD 5,000,000,000).

Nothing in this Agreement limits Provider's right to develop, market, license, host, or provide the Platform or any other product or service to any other person, including in any industry, vertical, or geography.

In response to Calloway's markup memorandum, the following issues were identified and addressed:

1. Uncapped liability for data, security, and privacy claims (§11.1): Escalated to the supervising lawyer due to the potential for unlimited exposure.

2. Ownership of feedback and integration work product (§6.1): Proposed a compromise where Meridian retains ownership but grants Calloway a perpetual, royalty-free license to use the work product.

3. Prohibition on training with Calloway data (§4.1, §4.3): Escalated to the supervising lawyer due to the significant impact on Meridian's ability to enhance the Platform.

4. On-site audit and inspection rights (§9.1): Asked the business team for clarification on the necessity of these rights and whether alternative assurances could be provided.

5. Retail-vertical exclusivity (§13.1): Escalated to the supervising lawyer due to the potential impact on Meridian's ability to serve other customers in the retail vertical.

Items requiring CEO sign-off include the uncapped liability for data, security, and privacy claims, prohibition on training with Calloway data, and retail-vertical exclusivity.

protocol.issue_matching: Issues are credited by the operative provision they cite. List the single provision your issue targets as the FIRST citation.
protocol.quotes: Optional 'quotes' entries must reproduce cited section text verbatim. A quotation that does not appear in the cited section is a critical failure.
protocol.questions: ask_client takes a natural-language question. Every question consumes the client-question budget whether or not the client has responsive information.
protocol.labels: issue_id is your own label. Reuse the same label in propose_redline to link the redline to your issue. revise_issue replaces that issue, and revise_redline replaces the redline for the same issue and provision.
protocol.escalation: Escalations are budgeted. Escalate departures from non-negotiable positions and requests beyond your authority. Both failing to escalate and over-escalating are scored.

read_document.description: Read a document from the matter file, either in full or one numbered section.

section.description: Optional section number such as '4.2'. Omit for full text.

search_matter.description: Case-insensitive substring search across every document section.

query.description: Search phrase, three or more characters.

ask_client.description: Ask the client one natural-language factual question. Every question consumes budget, so ask only questions that could change the negotiating position.

escalate.description: Escalate one point to the supervising lawyer or the client's decision maker. Every escalation consumes budget, so escalate only departures from a non-negotiable position or requests that exceed your authority.

topic.description: Short label for the point escalated.

reason.description: Why this exceeds your authority or departs from the playbook.

submit_issue.description: Submit one material issue. Cite the single operative provision the issue targets as the FIRST citation, in the form '<document_id> §<section>'. Optional quotes must reproduce cited section text verbatim.

issue_id.description: Your own short label for this issue; reuse it in propose_redline.

citations.description: Provision citations such as 'msa §4.2'. Operative provision first.

quotes.description: Optional verbatim quotations supporting the issue. Text must appear verbatim in the cited section; paraphrase belongs in analysis.

revise_issue.description: Replace a previously submitted issue with a revised version. The issue_id must identify an existing issue. Only the latest version is used for scoring.

issue_id.description: Label of the issue to revise.

propose_redline.description: Propose replacement language for one section. Target the operative provision of the issue; link it to your submitted issue by reusing your issue_id label.

issue_id.description: Label of your submitted issue.

revise_redline.description: Replace the latest redline for an existing issue and provision. Only the latest version for that issue/document/section target is used for scoring.

submit_final.description: Submit the final summary for the supervising lawyer and end the episode. Submit only after all issues and redlines are in.
